Package org.cyborgcats.component

Class Turret

java.lang.Object
org.cyborgcats.component.MotorComponent
org.cyborgcats.component.PositionComponent
org.cyborgcats.component.Turret
All Implemented Interfaces:
Component
public class Turret extends PositionComponent
Position component for a turret, adding absolute-position resolution from a pair of encoders and aiming helpers that compensate for robot motion.

The turret's absolute angle cannot be recovered from either encoder alone, since each wraps well before the turret completes a revolution. The two encoder gears have different tooth counts, so their combined readings identify a unique turret angle over the full travel range; this is resolved once at construction with a Chinese Remainder Theorem search. If no solution is found an Alert is raised and the turret keeps its power-on position.

The aiming helpers assume the turret's rotation axis is vertical, which holds while the robot is on flat ground; the tilted-chassis case is not yet implemented.

Commanded angles are wrapped into the range bounded by minAngle and maxAngle, so a target behind the turret is reached by continuing around rather than by reversing.

    • Turret

      public Turret(String name, double threshold, double debounceTime, Encoder encoderOne, Encoder encoderTwo, Range range, double tolerance, DriveState driveState, Pose3d turretOffset, MotorIOConfiguration leader)
      Constructs a Turret component and resolves its absolute starting position from both encoders.
      Parameters:
      name - unique name used as the AdvantageKit logging key under "mechanisms/"
      threshold - angular tolerance used to determine whether the turret is at a target position
      debounceTime - how long (in seconds) the turret must continuously be within threshold before the at-position check returns true
      encoderOne - encoder on the first reduction gear
      encoderTwo - encoder on the second reduction gear; must have a different tooth count than encoderOne for the CRT solve to be unique
      range - minimum and maximum angle the turret can rotate to
      tolerance - how close (in degrees) a CRT candidate must be to encoder two's reading to be accepted; size to the encoders' combined noise
      driveState - suppliers of the robot's field-relative chassis speeds and pose
      turretOffset - pose of the turret's rotation axis relative to the robot origin
      leader - configuration used to build the hardware interface for the turret motor

    • aimForTarget2D

      public Turret.TurretOutput aimForTarget2D(Pose2d targetPose, double tof)
      Returns both the turret setpoint and the shot distance for the given target, so callers that also drive a hood or flywheel do not have to recompute the aiming solution.

      The reported distance is measured from the turret's rotation axis to the motion-compensated virtual target, not to the target's true position, so it stays consistent with the angle the turret is being sent to. Carries the class-level flat-ground assumption and wraps the angle into the turret's range identically.

      Parameters:
      targetPose - the actual target pose on the field
      tof - expected projectile time-of-flight in seconds
      Returns:
      the turret setpoint and the range it was solved for

    • getVirtualTarget2D

      public static Translation2d getVirtualTarget2D(Pose2d targetPose, ChassisSpeeds speeds, double tof)
      Returns the field position to aim at so that a projectile still reaches the target despite the robot's own motion.

      The target is shifted against the robot's velocity multiplied by the time-of-flight, producing a "virtual target"; aiming at the virtual target cancels the velocity the projectile inherits from the robot. Because tof is supplied rather than derived, the caller is responsible for keeping it consistent with the resulting shot distance.

      The result is a field position, not a displacement, so it does not depend on where the robot sits; subtract the aiming origin from it to get the bearing and range. With a tof of zero it is exactly targetPose's translation.

      Parameters:
      targetPose - the actual target pose on the field
      speeds - current field-relative chassis speeds of the robot
      tof - expected projectile time-of-flight in seconds
      Returns:
      the field position of the motion-compensated virtual target

    • solveChineaseRemainderTherom

      public static Optional<Double> solveChineaseRemainderTherom(double a, double b, double e1ToothCount, double e2TootCount, double tolerance)
      Attempts to find the unique absolute turret angle (in degrees) that satisfies the readings from two encoders with different tooth counts relative to a 90-tooth turret gear.
      Parameters:
      a - normalised position reading from encoder 1 (range [0, 1))
      b - normalised position reading from encoder 2 (range [0, 1))
      e1ToothCount - tooth count of the first encoder gear
      e2TootCount - tooth count of the second encoder gear
      tolerance - how close the CRT candidate must be to encoder 2's effective reading (in degrees) to be accepted as a solution
      Returns:
      an Optional containing the resolved angle in degrees, or empty if no solution was found within the search range
